s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin lesions with atrophic and scar-like appearance on the face
salient_findings: Round atrophic lesions on the face
Lesions are symmetric and bilateral, located on the malar and preauricular areas
Histopathologic examination shows epidermal dell and superficial dermal lymphocytic infiltrate
key_facts: 26-year-old man with several-year history of skin lesions
Previous diagnosis and treatment were unsuccessful
No history of chicken pox, acne, or traumatic lesions in the affected areas
Lesions are 5 to 10 mm in diameter
Skin lesions are not indurated and display no epidermal changes
Histopathologic examination shows dermal fibrosis
Orcein stain demonstrates reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis
Lesions have a cicatricial appearance

shortlist.label: Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of atrophic skin lesions with a scar-like appearance on the face

shortlist.label: Mid-dermal elastolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathologic examination shows reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions have a cicatricial appearance and are atrophic, consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Anetoderma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of atrophic skin lesions with a loss of elastic fibers, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Atrophic lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Lesions are atrophic and have a scar-like appearance, consistent with this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of symmetric, bilateral, atrophic lesions on the face, especially on the malar and preauricular areas, with a diameter of 5 to 10 mm and a cicatricial appearance, along with histopathologic findings of epidermal dell, superficial dermal lymphocytic infiltrate, and reduction of elastic fibers in the dermis, is most consistent with Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini.

rejected.label: Mid-dermal elastolysis
rejected.why: While mid-dermal elastolysis also involves loss of elastic fibers, it typically presents with perifollicular papules and is not as commonly associated with the specific pattern of atrophy seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus
rejected.why: Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus often presents with more pronounced epidermal changes, such as scaling, and is typically found in the genital area, which does not match this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Anetoderma
rejected.why: Anetoderma is characterized by loss of elastic fibers but typically presents as outpouching of the skin rather than the atrophic, cicatricial lesions seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Atrophic lichen planus
rejected.why: Atrophic lichen planus would likely show more significant epidermal changes and is not as commonly associated with the specific pattern of elastic fiber loss and dermal fibrosis seen in this patient.
